handbookNote: Hawaii Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: PSI Services, LLC, under contract with the Hawaii Real Estate Commission (DCCA REB), per the official Candidate Information Bulletin (test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/1664, effective 1/16/2026). Uniform (national/general) portion: 75 scored items (worth 80 points -- some broker items are scored up to 2 points each, a real documented PSI scoring quirk unique to the broker exam), 150 minutes. Hawaii state portion (Broker): 50 items, 90 minutes. Combo: 125 items (130 points), 240 minutes. Passing score is a FLAT 75% for Brokers (Salesperson uses 70%), scored/passed independently per section -- a candidate who fails one section retakes only that section within 2 years. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=125, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=94 (round(125*0.75)), following the same 'literal-percent, section-independent-retake' convention as NE/AR (as distinct from UT/WV's scaled-score convention). NATIONAL PORTION (75 items, 11 sections) reuses the exact same real PSI national item bank/weights as Iowa and Mississippi (10/5/8/9/19/13/7/5/6/12/6 across Property Ownership/Land Use Controls/Valuation/Financing/Contracts/Agency/Property Disclosures/Property Management/Transfer of Title/Practice of Real Estate/Real Estate Calculations) -- confirmed identical via the official PSI bulletin's content outline. HAWAII STATE PORTION (50 items, real Broker item counts): Ascertaining and Disclosing Material Facts (7, incl. HRS Ch. 508D seller disclosure timelines, HARPTA 7.25% nonresident withholding under HRS 235-68, GET on commissions, the Bureau of Conveyances/Land Court dual recording system, and the 2022 Sea Level Rise Exposure Area disclosure law), Types of Ownership (3, HRS Ch. 514B condominiums, Ch. 514E timeshares, Ch. 421I cooperative housing corporations, and Hawaii's distinctive large-private-landowner leasehold history incl. Hawaii Housing Authority v. Midkiff), Property Management (5, incl. HRS Ch. 521 Residential Landlord-Tenant Code -- notably the 2025 Act 278 amendment to HRS 521-68 effective 2/5/2026 replacing the old 5-business-day nonpayment demand with a 10-calendar-day notice plus mandatory mediation-center referral -- and broker-only commercial management/trust-account supervision duties), Land Utilization (3, HRS Ch. 205's real statewide four-district land use classification system unique to Hawaii -- Urban/Rural/Agricultural/Conservation -- plus HRS Ch. 205A Special Management Area coastal permitting), Title and Conveyances (6, Hawaii's real dual recording system -- the 'regular system' HRS Ch. 502 race-notice recording vs. the Land Court/Torrens system HRS Ch. 501 with indefeasible Certificates of Title -- plus mechanic's liens, kuleana land history, and both judicial and nonjudicial foreclosure under HRS Ch. 667), Contracts (7, HRS Ch. 508D disclosure-to-contract timing incl. the 10-day delivery/15-day rescission windows, the real Agreement of Sale seller-financing instrument under HRS 502-85, and broker supervisory review duties under HRS 467-1.6), Financing (2, the Agreement of Sale/PMM seller-financing instruments and Hawaii's leasehold-lending term constraint), Escrow Process and Closing Statements (4, Hawaii's real HRS Ch. 449-licensed independent escrow-depository closing practice -- regulated by DCCA's Division of Financial Institutions, not the Real Estate Commission), and Professional Practices and Conduct (13, largest state section -- trust account rules under HAR 16-99-4, the real Recovery Fund figures under HRS 467-16 ($25,000/transaction) and 467-24 ($50,000/licensee aggregate) with the 467-17 replenishment-below-$350,000 trigger, the full HRS 467-14 22-item disciplinary grounds list, the HRS 467-9.5(a)(4)(B) broker-experience prerequisite (3 of the most recent 5 years full-time licensed salesperson experience, HAR 16-99-19.2's 40-hr/week full-time definition), independent-contractor-vs-employee treatment under HRS 467-1.5, office/branch-office rules under HRS 467-12, and advertising rules under HAR 16-99-11). Governing law: HRS Chapter 467 (Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons), HRS Chapter 436B (Professional and Vocational Licensing Law), and Hawaii Administrative Rules Title 16, Chapter 99. This bank was drafted across 9 new state-topic drafting passes (the 11 national files were reused from ia_re_broker_questions/ms_re_broker_questions, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
